name: Bellhop Redis store behaviour
description: The behaviour specific to the Redis store and Redis-compatible servers: server detection, durability and eviction warnings, recovery from a flush or reset, capability reporting, ShardByQueue scope and hybrid notifications. The command set, data model, Lua rules, topologies and server versions are technical specifications (TECH-52 to TECH-87).

entities.name: RedisStore
entities.description: The Redis store as seen by one node.

ears.when: the connection is established and a trivial EVAL script succeeds
ears.shall: identify the server family and version from HELLO and INFO, apply that family's adjustments if the family is recognised, mark the store ready and show the family and version in the startup summary

requirements.notes: Valkey reports redis_version 7.2.4 in INFO, so detection must use HELLO (RDV-1). Families: Redis, Valkey, Garnet, Dragonfly, Kvrocks, KeyDB, Redict, unknown. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-12 (recommended option): this runs on every connection, including a reconnection after REQ-529, so a failover re-checks the new primary; an unrecognised family gets no adjustments (REQ-501).

ears.when: the connection is established and a trivial EVAL script succeeds
ears.if: the server family is not recognised
ears.shall: log a warning that names what was detected and continue

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-500 with an extra consequence.

sources.quote: An unknown family is allowed with a warning

ears.while: a node using the Redis store is starting
ears.if: the server does not support EVAL
ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that names the server flag that enables scripting, such as --lua on Garnet

sources.quote: a missing EVAL is a startup failure with a message naming the server flag to enable it

ears.when: the store becomes ready after a connection to the server
ears.if: INFO persistence shows that AOF is off, or the server persists by snapshot only
ears.shall: log a warning that acknowledged jobs can be lost in a crash, naming the server's durability flag where one exists, such as --aof-commit-wait on Garnet

requirements.notes: If INFO persistence is not available on the server, the source says 'where available'; what to log then is open. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-12 (recommended option): logged after every connection or reconnection (REQ-500, REQ-529), not when reconciliation makes the store ready again (REQ-509).

ears.when: the store becomes ready after a connection to the server
ears.shall: log a notice that replication is asynchronous and a failover can drop acknowledged writes

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-12 (recommended option): logged after every connection or reconnection (REQ-500, REQ-529), not when reconciliation makes the store ready again (REQ-509).

ears.while: a node using the Redis store is starting
ears.if: maxmemory-policy is anything other than noeviction
ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that eviction can silently delete job data without any reset being detected, naming the maxmemory-policy setting

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 option 1 (owner's decision on 2026-11-06: full protection): was a warning. Eviction removes keys one at a time and leaves the generation marker in place, so it can lose outcomes and recurring definitions with no reset ever detected. Cost: servers whose eviction policy cannot be changed are refused. A failover to a server with another policy is reported by REQ-531.

ears.shall: include the persistence mode in the health check and report used_memory against maxmemory

requirements.notes: used_memory reporting is SHOULD (RED-13); the persistence mode is MUST (RED-7). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the check turns Degraded above 80% of maxmemory (REQ-519, REQ-520).

ears.while: the store is ready or reconciling
ears.when: any read this node makes of the generation marker, including those of its claim, heartbeat and completion scripts, finds it missing, or with a value older than the last value this node saw, whether or not it is flagged as reconciling
ears.if: this node has seen a generation marker since it started
ears.shall: replace the marker, in the same atomic step as the read that found it, with the Redis server's current time as both its value and its last-reset value, flagged as reconciling, log the ERROR event StoreWasReset, and start re-seeding the code-defined recurring jobs, the queue registry and this node's registration

requirements.notes: Causes: FLUSHALL, a restore from an old snapshot, a failover to a lagging replica (both bring back an older marker). Partial eviction is excluded by REQ-505. A run whose job record vanished re-creates it at its next heartbeat (REQ-522) or completion (REQ-521). Runtime-defined recurring jobs cannot be re-seeded; the loss is reported and health stays Degraded until an operator acknowledges it (REQ-523 to REQ-525). refiner-model 2026-11-06: F-2 option 1 (owner's decision: full protection) adds the 'older' test, with the marker advanced every RecurringReconcileInterval (REQ-527); a rollback to a state less than one interval old is not detected. F-3 (recommended): only a node that has seen a marker reports a reset; a new server is initialised by REQ-528. F-4 (recommended): detection and reconciliation are worker duties, matching hosting REQ-40. F-8 (recommended): the reconciling marker is written at detection, so a second flush during reconciliation removes it and is detected again. F-9 (recommended): the compare-and-set makes exactly one node report each reset; the others reconcile silently. F-13 (recommended): the node registration is re-seeded too, so the orphan sweep (recurring REQ-205, REQ-207) does not act on the re-seeded jobs. Run 2: F-1 (recommended), a flagged marker is judged too, so the lowest-value first marker a late node writes after a flush (REQ-528) is still found older and reported. F-6 (recommended), values come from the server clock, which keeps moving across a flush, so no two nodes pick values that go backwards relative to each other and report a phantom reset; a failover to a server whose clock is behind looks like a rollback and is reported as a reset (NFR-31). F-5 (option 2, accepted): after a rollback to older data, jobs claimed since that copy may run again and their outcomes may be lost until a node detects it; this is at-least-once, like a lost lease, and is reported. Closing it fully is impossible, since a rollback within one RecurringReconcileInterval is not detected at all. Run 4 F-1 (recommended option): every marker read the node already makes is a detection point, not a separate look at some unspecified time. The claim script reads the marker every PollInterval and the heartbeat every HeartbeatInterval, so a node that is working sees a flush well within REQ-509's wait of one LeaseDuration, before REQ-527 can advance the lowest-value marker of REQ-528 away. Before, a node could claim and heartbeat under that marker without detecting it, and the flush stayed hidden with no node paused. Only a node that makes no read for the whole window misses it, and its runs have lost their lease; that is the case REQ-528's notes and NFR-31 accept. Run 5 F-1 (recommended option): the write is made in the same atomic step as the read that found the marker missing or older (the same script, TECH-130). Run 4 moved that read into the scripts, which left the compare-and-set as a later command, and it could lose to REQ-528's first marker or REQ-527's advance; neither reports, so the loser re-seeded silently and the flush went unreported although this node had read it. With the read and the write in one step nothing can land between them, the write always succeeds, and every other node finds the new flagged value and joins silently (REQ-530). F-9's 'exactly one node reports each reset' now follows from that, with no compare-and-set. Not chosen: retrying a lost compare-and-set (a second rule with a subtle last-reset test), or replacing REQ-528's lowest-value marker with an 'initialised without a report' mark (run 3 F-3 already declined a second detection trigger).

ears.if: no check that reports Unhealthy fails
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5 and F-6 (recommended option): the guard gives Unhealthy precedence on the same health-check run, as hosting REQ-34 does, and from Unhealthy lets a node whose store came back drop to Degraded instead of staying Unhealthy. Run 2: since F-1 a new server is reconciled too (REQ-528), and claims are paused either way, so the node reports Degraded during any reconciliation; Degraded does not fail a readiness probe.

sources.quote: the health check turns degraded until reconciliation completes

ears.when: this node has re-seeded the code-defined recurring jobs, the queue registry and its registration, and LeaseDuration has passed since it last started re-seeding (REQ-507, REQ-528, REQ-530)
ears.shall: clear the reconciling flag on the generation marker if it is still set on the value this reconciliation is for, and mark the store ready

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06: F-8 (recommended) moves writing the new marker to detection (REQ-507), so this only clears the flag. F-1 option 1 (owner's decision: full protection): waiting HeartbeatInterval gives every live run one heartbeat to re-create its record and concurrency-key hold (REQ-522) before claims resume (REQ-526). Cost: claims pause for about 20 s after a reset. Run 2 F-3 (recommended option): the wait is a full LeaseDuration, measured from when this node's store became reconciling, which a reconnection restarts (REQ-529, REQ-530). The rule is that a detected flush ends every lease: the flag is never cleared less than one lease after it was set, so a run that could not re-assert its record in that time would have lost its lease without any reset (jobs REQ-132) and is treated the same way. Cost: claims pause for about 60 s after a reset, and for the same time when the first worker starts on a new server (REQ-528). Run 3 F-1 (recommended option): the wait restarts every time this node starts re-seeding, a second detection while already reconciling included. Measured from the store becoming reconciling, a second flush caught mid-reconciliation inherited a wait that was already over, so its flag was cleared at once beside a run that had kept its lease.

ears.when: RecurringReconcileInterval, 5 minutes by default, has passed since the last reconciliation
ears.shall: reconcile the code-defined recurring jobs again so that a flush never silently stops them

ears.while: the generation marker is flagged as reconciling and a node with the worker registered is running
ears.shall: eventually re-seed every code-defined recurring job and clear the reconciling flag

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-4 (recommended option): re-seeding is a worker duty (hosting REQ-40), so only a running worker node is obliged; a client-only node never starts a reconciliation (REQ-507). Clearing the flag matters because claims are paused while it is set (REQ-526).

sources.quote: a flush never silently stops them

ears.while: the generation marker is missing and a node with the worker registered is running
ears.shall: eventually write a generation marker

requirements.rationale: Claims are paused while the marker is missing (REQ-526), so a missing marker must not last.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 and F-3 (owner's decision and recommended option).

ears.where: the server runs standalone, as primary and replica with Sentinel, or as a Cluster
ears.shall: start and run without refusing the topology

requirements.rationale: Correctness comes from one atomic script per transition (TECH-57), not from refusing to start.

sources.quote: The store MUST NOT fail closed on a topology it recognises

ears.shall: enforce unique keys per queue rather than per namespace

requirements.notes: This weakens INV-100: two active jobs with the same unique key can exist in different queues.

sources.quote: in that mode uniqueness scope is per queue

ears.shall: report in the Redis store's capability set no transactional enqueue, while offering push notifications and result storage

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: free-text payload search is dropped from Bellhop altogether as overkill; tag filters (BLT-9) cover looking jobs up by business key. Checked against current Redis: pub/sub gives push notifications and hashes with TTLs give result storage on every supported server, while no Redis server can join the application's SQL transaction. Redis 8 does ship a query engine with full-text search, but it is not used (RDV-2).

ears.shall: lower the default payload hard limit to 256 KB on the Redis store
cap the size of captured logs and job results and give them the same TTL as their job's record, renewed whenever the job changes state

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11 (recommended option): a fixed TTL could expire logs before a long-kept job, such as a dead letter kept 30 days (jobs REQ-104), against jobs INV-119.

ears.when: a node has not sent a heartbeat for longer than StaleNodeAge
ears.shall: remove its node registration

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-14 (recommended option): an event that removes the node from the store's view, so a transition rather than an invariant; the age is the new assumption REQ-533. Jobs REQ-124 (Unroutable) and recurring REQ-205 (Orphaned) count running worker nodes from these registrations.

ears.where: UseRedisNotifications() pairs a SQL store with Redis
ears.when: a job is enqueued
ears.shall: publish a wake-up signal on Redis so other nodes pick up work without waiting for the next poll

ears.where: UseRedisNotifications() pairs a SQL store with Redis
ears.shall: keep processing by polling the SQL store at PollInterval

sources.quote: if it is unavailable the SQL store falls back to polling

ears.where: UseRedisNotifications() pairs a SQL store with Redis
ears.shall: never read job state from Redis; the SQL store is the only source of truth

sources.quote: Redis is then a signal, never a source of truth

ears.shall: not test or document Tendis, Pika/PikiwiDB or other region-specific forks, but accept reports about them

ears.when: the health check runs
ears.if: no check that reports Unhealthy fails and the Redis server's used_memory is above RedisMemoryDegradedShare of its maxmemory
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: an eviction is a store reset in disguise, so warn early. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5 and F-6 (recommended option): Unhealthy takes precedence on the same run, and a node recovering from Unhealthy drops to Degraded.

ears.shall: default RedisMemoryDegradedShare to 80% (RedisMemoryDegradedShare)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.when: a run completes or fails, its job's record no longer exists and the store was reset since the claim
ears.shall: write a minimal job record with the job's id, name, outcome and node, marked as recreated after a store reset, and log a warning

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 so the outcome is not lost from history. This is not a stale token in the sense of jobs INV-128: there is no current record to protect. A record missing for any other reason is still refused. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 option 1 (owner's decision: full protection): 'the store was reset since the claim' is defined in the glossary (resetSinceClaim) and now also covers a marker older than at the claim and a reset detected in between, so a second flush or a rollback no longer loses the outcome. Runs that heartbeat before completing have already re-created their record (REQ-522). Run 2 F-3: the marker's last-reset value (REQ-507) also covers a run on a node that missed the whole reconciliation, for example behind an outage, so its outcome is recorded rather than lost. Run 3 F-3: REQ-528's first marker has a last-reset value too, so this also covers a run that missed a reconciliation a late node started. Run 4 F-2 (recommended option): the glossary compares the marker's last-reset value with the last-reset value read at the claim, not with the marker value. REQ-528's first marker has a value (the lowest) older than its last-reset time, so the old comparison counted every job claimed under it as reset since the claim, and a deleted job could come back here with a reset logged that never happened.

ears.while: the generation marker is missing or flagged as reconciling
ears.if: a heartbeat or progress write finds its job's record missing, the store was reset since the claim, and the run's leaseExpiresAt has not passed according to the database clock
ears.shall: re-create the job's record as processing with the run's claiming node, leaseToken, leaseExpiresAt, queue, concurrency key, unique key and recurring occurrence, so that queue limits, concurrency keys, unique keys and recurring overlap count the run again, and let the run continue

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 that the run continues; the result is recorded at completion (REQ-521). refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 option 1 (owner's decision: full protection): the heartbeat re-creates the record instead of being ignored, so a second job with the same concurrency key, queue limit or recurring job is not admitted beside the old run (jobs INV-107, INV-108, recurring INV-204). Claims stay paused until every live run has had one heartbeat (REQ-509, REQ-526). Run 2: F-2, the unique key is re-created too, and a job that took it during the pause is cancelled (REQ-534). F-3, the record is re-created only while the reconciliation lasts. After it, a run that never re-asserted is treated like any run whose lease expired: its heartbeat re-creates nothing, so it never becomes a second holder beside a job claimed after the pause, and its outcome is still recorded when it finishes (REQ-521). Run 3 F-2 (recommended option): the run's own lease decides, not only the marker's state. A run whose lease expired during one reconciliation was excluded only because the flag was no longer set; a later flush set it again and the run came back as a second Processing occurrence or a second holder of a unique key. With the test, a run that could not re-assert in time stays expired at every later reset, as under jobs REQ-132, and its outcome is still recorded (REQ-521).

ears.when: this node's compare-and-set in REQ-507 succeeds
ears.shall: log an ERROR saying that runtime-defined recurring jobs, the maintenance pause, queue pauses, runtime throttle limits and recurring-job pauses may have been lost and are back at their defaults, record the reset as unacknowledged in the store, and remember it until it finds the reset acknowledged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: report only; nodes do not cache runtime definitions. refiner-model 2026-11-06: F-7 (recommended) lists every piece of operator state that falls back to its default; a paused code-defined recurring job is re-seeded as Active. F-8 (recommended): the record is kept in the store and re-written by REQ-532 if a later flush erases it. F-9 (recommended): only the node that wins the compare-and-set reports the reset. Run 3 F-5 (recommended option): the trigger names REQ-507, because REQ-528's first write is also a compare-and-set of a reconciling marker and must not report a reset (SCN-503).

ears.when: the health check runs
ears.if: no check that reports Unhealthy fails and a store reset has not been acknowledged
ears.shall: report the node Degraded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Lasts beyond reconciliation (REQ-508), until an operator acknowledges the reset (REQ-525). refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5 and F-6 (recommended option): Unhealthy takes precedence on the same run, and a node recovering from Unhealthy drops to Degraded.

ears.when: an operator acknowledges a store reset on the dashboard
ears.shall: record the reset as acknowledged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Acknowledging is an operate action (dashboard INV-301).

ears.while: the generation marker is missing or flagged as reconciling
ears.shall: claim no job and create no recurring occurrence

requirements.rationale: Holds erased by a flush must be re-asserted (REQ-522) before new holders are admitted, or two jobs run under a Max = 1 concurrency key (jobs INV-107, INV-108, recurring INV-204).
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 option 1 (owner's decision on 2026-11-06: full protection). The claim script checks the marker itself, so claims stop the moment a flush removes it, before any node has detected the reset. A new server claims nothing until a worker node writes the first marker (REQ-528). A rollback that brings back an older marker is caught only when a node detects it (REQ-507). Run 2 F-2 (recommended in part): the scheduler creates no occurrence during the pause, because recurring overlap (INV-204) decides by looking for an unfinished job that the flush erased; instants that fall due meanwhile are handled by the misfire policy when the pause ends (recurring REQ-217 to REQ-219). Enqueues are not held, not even with a unique key; REQ-534 resolves a unique-key collision instead. A continuation added to a running job during the pause can be refused as having no parent (jobs INV-138) until the job re-asserts its record. F-5 (option 2, accepted): until a node detects a rollback, claims go on against the restored data, so jobs claimed since that copy may run again (NFR-31).

ears.when: RecurringReconcileInterval has passed since the generation marker was last advanced
ears.shall: advance the unflagged generation marker to the Redis server's current time by compare-and-set, unless another node already did, and remember the value

requirements.rationale: A restore or failover brings back an older marker; only a marker that moves forward reveals the rollback (REQ-507).
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 option 1 (owner's decision on 2026-11-06: full protection). Part of the Redis recurring reconciliation duty, so worker nodes only (hosting REQ-40). Every node remembers the latest marker value it reads (lastSeenMarker). Cost: one write per interval. Run 2 F-6 (recommended option): the server clock, not the node's memory, makes every new value later than any written before; the last-reset value is left as it is.

ears.when: any read this node makes of the generation marker, including those of its claim, heartbeat and completion scripts, finds it missing
ears.if: this node has not seen a generation marker since it started
ears.shall: write the first generation marker at the lowest value, with the Redis server's current time as its last-reset value, flagged as reconciling, in the same atomic step as the read that found it missing, log at INFO that it initialised the store and that claims start when the reconciliation ends, and start re-seeding the code-defined recurring jobs, the queue registry and this node's registration without logging StoreWasReset or recording the reset as unacknowledged

requirements.rationale: An empty server and a flushed one look the same; a new installation must not be reported as a reset.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3 (recommended option). Same event as REQ-507 for a node that has not seen a marker. A flush that happens while every worker is down is still reported if a node that saw the old marker comes back: it finds this lowest-value marker older than the one it saw (REQ-507). It goes unreported if no running node saw a marker before, or if every node that did misses this marker until it is advanced (run 3 F-3). Run 2 F-1 (recommended option): a flushed server looks exactly like a new one, and the first node to look may be one that started moments after the flush while another node is still running a job. The first marker is therefore flagged and reconciled (REQ-509): claims stay paused for one lease, running jobs re-assert their holds, and a node that saw an earlier marker still finds this one older and reports the reset (REQ-507). Cost: on a new server the first claim waits one LeaseDuration (60 s); tests against a fresh Redis can lower LeaseDuration (NFR-31). If another node replaces the marker meanwhile, this node finishes its wait, then joins the new value through REQ-530. Run 3 F-3 (option 2): the first marker carries the server's current time as its last-reset value, so a run claimed under an earlier marker on a node that missed this whole reconciliation still has its outcome recorded (REQ-521, glossary resetSinceClaim). The flush itself is reported only if a node that saw the earlier marker reads this one before REQ-527 advances it; a node paused for that whole time (more than one LeaseDuration, so its runs are lease-lost anyway) does not report it, and NFR-31 says so. Not chosen: letting such a node detect it later, which needs every node to remember a second value and a third detection trigger, and would start a second cluster-wide pause when the paused node wakes. Run 4 F-1: 'reads this one' means any marker read, including the claim and heartbeat scripts (REQ-507), so 'paused' means making no marker read for the whole window. Run 5 F-1: the write is atomic with the read that found the marker missing, like REQ-507's, so 'only if none exists yet' holds by construction and no other write can land between them.

ears.when: the connection to the server is lost or the server's role changes
ears.shall: mark the store connecting and repeat server detection when it reconnects

requirements.rationale: After a failover the new primary's family, persistence and eviction settings must be checked again (REQ-500 to REQ-504, REQ-531).
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-12 (recommended option). A node that was reconciling resumes through REQ-530 after reconnecting, because the marker is still flagged. Run 2 F-3/F-4: it rejoins even if it had already re-seeded for that value, and its wait in REQ-509 starts again from the reconnection.

ears.when: any read this node makes of the generation marker, including those of its claim, heartbeat and completion scripts, finds it flagged as reconciling with a value whose reconciliation this node has not finished
ears.if: that value is not older than the last value this node saw
ears.shall: start re-seeding the code-defined recurring jobs, the queue registry and this node's registration without logging StoreWasReset, and remember the value

requirements.rationale: Every worker re-seeds what its own code declares and its own registration; only the node that detected the reset reports it.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9 and F-13 (recommended options): the nodes that lose the compare-and-set in REQ-507, or check the marker after it was written, reconcile silently. Also resumes a reconciliation interrupted by a reconnection (REQ-529, F-12). Run 2 F-4 (recommended option): a node has finished a value's reconciliation once it cleared the flag on it (REQ-509) or found the marker no longer flagged with it. Before, a reconnection after re-seeding but before the clear left the flag set for good and blocked every claim; re-seeding again is idempotent and costs little. Run 3 F-4 (recommended option): a flagged marker older than the last value this node saw is a reset this node must report (REQ-507), not a reconciliation to join. Without the guard both sentences applied, and joining silently made the node remember the lower value, so the flush was never reported. Run 4 F-1: the same marker reads as REQ-507 drive this sentence, so one check on every read covers REQ-507, REQ-528 and REQ-530. Run 5 F-1: REQ-507's write is atomic with its read, so no node loses it; the other nodes find the new flagged value and join here.

ears.when: the store becomes ready after a connection to the server
ears.if: maxmemory-policy is anything other than noeviction
ears.shall: log an ERROR that the server may evict job data and that resets caused by eviction are not detected

requirements.rationale: REQ-505 refuses such a server at startup; a failover can still land a running node on one.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 option 1 and F-12 (recommended option). Same event as REQ-503 and REQ-504.

ears.while: this node remembers an unacknowledged store reset
ears.if: the store holds no record of that reset
ears.shall: re-write the record as unacknowledged

requirements.rationale: A later flush must not erase the only trace of an unacknowledged reset.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8 (recommended option). A node forgets the reset once it finds it acknowledged (REQ-523, REQ-525). The record does not survive a flush while every node that remembers it is down.

ears.shall: default StaleNodeAge to 3 × HeartbeatInterval, 60 seconds (StaleNodeAge)

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-14 (recommended option). HeartbeatInterval is jobs REQ-102 (20 s). The owner may prefer another value; note that jobs REQ-124 and recurring REQ-205 act on a node as soon as its registration is gone, while integrations NodeLostAfter (5 minutes) is longer.

ears.when: a run's job record is re-created after a store reset (REQ-522) with a unique key that another active job holds
ears.shall: cancel that other job with reason DuplicateAfterReset in the same write that re-creates the record

requirements.rationale: A flush erases a running job's unique-key lock, so an enqueue with the same key succeeds before the run's next heartbeat re-creates its record, leaving two active jobs with one key (jobs INV-100).
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-2, chosen instead of the recommended hold on unique-key enqueues. Holding would make every enqueue with a unique key block for up to a lease and then fail during a reset, and on a new server with no worker running yet, where nothing can collide. Before the flush the key belonged to the running job, so the other holder was created during the pause, and claims are paused (REQ-526), so it has never run. Cancelling it gives the state the store would have had without the flush; the caller was told the job was enqueued, and its cancel reason says why.

scenarios.title: FLUSHALL is detected and recurring jobs come back
scenarios.given: Worker node n1 runs against the ready Redis store, has seen its generation marker, and code-defined recurring job nightly-cleanup exists; someone runs FLUSHALL.

steps.note: marker missing; n1 writes the reconciling marker and logs StoreWasReset
ERROR listing what may have been lost; reset recorded as unacknowledged
health Degraded
re-seeded; after LeaseDuration the reconciling flag is cleared

scenarios.then: nightly-cleanup exists again, the generation marker is present without the reconciling flag, the store is Ready, one ERROR StoreWasReset event and one ERROR listing what may have been lost were logged, no job was claimed while the marker was missing or flagged, and health stays Degraded until an operator acknowledges the reset.

steps.note: store tries to become ready

scenarios.title: Hybrid notifications survive a Redis outage
scenarios.given: SQL Server store with UseRedisNotifications(); Redis goes down; a job is enqueued on node A.
scenarios.then: Node B picks up the job within PollInterval by polling SQL Server, and no job state was read from Redis.

scenarios.title: A new Redis server is initialised, not reported as a reset
scenarios.given: Worker node n1 starts against an empty Redis server; no node has seen a generation marker.

steps.note: store ready
first marker written flagged as reconciling, INFO logged
re-seeded; after LeaseDuration the reconciling flag is cleared

scenarios.then: A generation marker exists without the reconciling flag, no StoreWasReset event or reset ERROR was logged, no reset is recorded as unacknowledged, and claims are allowed.

scenarios.title: A run keeps its concurrency-key hold across a flush
scenarios.given: Worker nodes n1 and n2 run; n1 is processing j1 with concurrency key tenant:42 (Max = 1); someone runs FLUSHALL; then j2 with key tenant:42 is enqueued.

steps.note: n2 detects the missing marker and writes the reconciling marker
j1's next heartbeat re-creates its record as Processing with its hold on tenant:42
after LeaseDuration the reconciling flag is cleared

scenarios.then: j1 is Processing and holds tenant:42, j2 has not been claimed, and no job was claimed while the marker was missing or flagged.

scenarios.title: A restore from an older snapshot is detected
scenarios.given: Worker node n1 last saw generation marker value 7; the Redis server is restored from a snapshot taken when the marker was 5.

steps.note: marker older than the last value seen

scenarios.then: n1 logged StoreWasReset, the marker has a value later than 7 and is flagged as reconciling, and n1 is re-seeding.

scenarios.title: A client-only node does not start a reconciliation
scenarios.given: Client-only node n2 (no worker registered) runs against the ready Redis store and has seen its generation marker; someone runs FLUSHALL.

steps.note: n2 finds the marker missing

scenarios.title: A node that first looks after a flush does not end the pause
scenarios.given: Worker node n1 has seen the generation marker and is processing j1 with concurrency key tenant:42 (Max = 1). Worker node n2 has started but has not read the marker yet. Someone runs FLUSHALL.

steps.note: n2 finds the marker missing, has never seen one, and writes the lowest value flagged as reconciling
n1 finds the lowest value older than the one it saw, writes a new flagged value and logs StoreWasReset
j1's next heartbeat re-creates its record as Processing with its hold on tenant:42
after LeaseDuration the reconciling flag is cleared

scenarios.then: One StoreWasReset event was logged, j1 is Processing and holds tenant:42, and no job was claimed while the marker was missing or flagged.

scenarios.title: A unique-key duplicate created during the pause is cancelled
scenarios.given: Worker node n1 is processing j1 with unique key invoice:7. Someone runs FLUSHALL, and the application then enqueues j2 with unique key invoice:7, which the store accepts because the lock is gone.

steps.note: n1 detects the reset and writes the reconciling marker
j1's next heartbeat re-creates its record as Processing with invoice:7
j2 is cancelled with reason DuplicateAfterReset in the same write

scenarios.then: j1 is Processing and holds invoice:7, j2 is Cancelled with reason DuplicateAfterReset and was never claimed, and at no moment did two active jobs hold invoice:7.

scenarios.title: A second flush during reconciliation restarts the wait
scenarios.given: Worker nodes n1 and n2 have seen the generation marker. n2 is processing j1 with concurrency key tenant:42 and Max = 1. Someone runs FLUSHALL.

steps.note: n1 detects the reset, writes flagged value T1 and starts re-seeding
j1's next heartbeat re-creates its record with its tenant:42 hold
LeaseDuration after step 1, before n1 has finished re-seeding, a second FLUSHALL; n1 finds the marker missing, writes flagged value T2 and starts re-seeding again
n1 finishes re-seeding and clears the flag on T2 at once

scenarios.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-07 run 3 F-1 regression: the flag on T2 stays until one LeaseDuration after step 3, so j1 can re-assert before tenant:42 can be claimed again.

scenarios.title: A run whose lease expired is not brought back by a later flush
scenarios.given: Worker nodes n1 and n2 have seen the generation marker. n2 is processing j1, an occurrence of nightly-cleanup with overlap Skip. Someone runs FLUSHALL, and n2 then pauses for longer than LeaseDuration.

steps.note: n1 detects the reset and starts re-seeding
LeaseDuration later n1 clears the flag; j1 never re-asserted, so its lease has expired
a second FLUSHALL; n1 detects it and writes a new flagged marker
n2 resumes and j1's heartbeat tries to re-create its record as processing

scenarios.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-07 run 3 F-2 regression: j1's outcome is still recorded at completion (REQ-521).

glossary.generationMarker: A key holding a value that only moves forward, a reconciling flag and the value of the last reset. A worker node writes the first one on a new server at the lowest value, flagged, with the server's current time as its last reset (REQ-528), advances it to the Redis server's current time every RecurringReconcileInterval (REQ-527), and replaces it with the server's current time, flagged and recorded as the last reset, when it detects a reset (REQ-507); the flag is cleared one LeaseDuration after this node last started re-seeding (REQ-509). Every node remembers the last value it saw (lastSeenMarker).
glossary.RedisMemoryDegradedShare: Share of maxmemory above which health reports Degraded; 80% by default (REQ-520).
glossary.ShardByQueue: Opt-in Cluster mode with one hash tag per queue instead of per namespace (INV-500).
glossary.StaleNodeAge: How long a node may go without a heartbeat before its registration is removed; 3 × HeartbeatInterval, 60 s by default (REQ-533).
glossary.resetSinceClaim: The store was reset since a job was claimed: the generation marker is missing, flagged as reconciling, or older than the value read when the job was claimed, or the marker's last-reset value is later than the last-reset value read when the job was claimed, or this node has detected or learned of a reset since the claim (REQ-507, REQ-530). Used by REQ-521 and REQ-522 as 'the store was reset since the claim'.
